notes:
Overview: Aurum is a mid-to-large tier payments platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive fraud scoring + merchant support features. Primary ask: deterministically bounded tail latency under sustained throughput; clear measurement spec for contract.

POC scope: reserved GPU pool (8xA100) with production-like traffic replay (mix of short chat queries 8-64 tokens and reranking jobs 256-1024 tokens). Evaluate both streaming and non-streaming paths.

SLO targets discussed: p50/p95/p99 for server-side request completion and per-token streaming latency. Initial target suggestions from Aurum: non-streaming p95 <= 150ms for 512-token context (inference-only, excludes network) and p99 <= 400ms; streaming token latency <= 30ms median and p95 <= 120ms. They emphasized client-side observed latency must be honored: want guidance on how to account for TLS handshake, CDN/edge, and client render.

Measurement alignment issues (current negotiation points):
- Client vs server timing: Aurum measures end-to-end client RTT (app-level). Redwood measures server-side inference time (handler entry -> final token). Need mutual spec: record both; define SLA on server-side p95/p99 with max allowed client-side network overhead.
- Streaming semantics: whether token emission latency measured from server token availability or from first byte at client. For SLOs, propose split metrics: server-token-latency and client-token-latency.
- Batching and KV cache effects: POC will include cold-cache, warm-cache, and mixed prefix reuse scenarios. Aurum wants deterministic worst-case for cold-cache to feed SLA/risk models.
- Throughput guarantees: baseline steady-state 500 reqs/s (non-streaming) with 2x burst to 1,200 reqs/s for short windows. Need capacity profile + autoscale headroom defined in SLA.

Recent timeline: 
- 2026-02-20: Intro call (Samira) — Aurum shares high-level constraints and compliance posture.
- 2026-02-27: Security questionnaire submitted by Aurum; Redwood to provide SOC2 artifacts. (INF-1043 opened)
- 2026-03-02: Deep-dive SLO workshop (Diego + engineering) — captured in ff-20260302-aurum-eval-call transcript. Agreed to measurable definitions to iterate on.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing + architecture deck shared (drive:/decks/aurum/dedicated-eval-v2.pptx).
- 2026-03-10: Kickoff for traffic-shaped POC; initial results scheduled after 2 business days of run.

Acceptance criteria for POC / eval: 
- Redwood provides a measurement spec (CSV+Grafana) that maps server-side timers to client-observed metrics; includes definitions for p50/p95/p99 for both streaming tokens and non-streaming completion.
- POC demonstrates sustained 500 reqs/s with non-streaming p95 < 150ms for 512-token synthetic workload AND a documented plan for cold-cache spikes.
- Logging & audit: KMS integrated for keys, audit events forwarded to Aurum SIEM, retention baseline agreed (90 days).

Negotiation notes / redlines expected for contract: 
- Precise SLA language on "latency" must reference server-side measurement method and specify allowed network delta. Aurum will not agree to opaque "end-to-end" wording without test harness.
- Credits for SLO misses: prefer service credits tied to p99 misses during steady-state (not burst windows).
- Capacity reservation: dispute around how much headroom Redwood must maintain for autoscale; Aurum pushing for 25% reserved headroom for peak.

Next steps (short):

- POC to run 2026-03-11 -> 2026-03-24 (traffic-shaped). Redwood SE to instrument client-side test harness.
- Diego to schedule final SLA review meeting wk of 2026-03-22.

- Very compliance-heavy; on-prem packaged insinuates long procurement.
- "We need the numbers — give us server timers + reproducible test harness" — quoted from CTO call.
